From: Anna Lopez <anna@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SaaS contract: metering & entitlement mapping (ACME)

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send the current SaaS master agreement and a short note on how ACME expects usage to be metered for billing. I attached the current contract (acme_saas_contract_v1.pdf) and a quick internal note on our expected license granularity.

Two quick asks so we can complete the procurement checklist on our side: 
- Can you share a sample invoice or billing CSV that shows how Redwood maps entitlements (product SKUs / tenant IDs) to metered usage?
- Do you have a standard fulfillment flow for AWS Marketplace (SaaS): entitlement activation, webhook examples, and time-to-activate after purchase?

Procurement would like to see the invoice sample and the entitlement mapping before signing — they use it to validate the finance handoff.

Thanks,
Anna Lopez
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_saas_contract_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SaaS contract: metering & entitlement mapping (ACME)

Hi Anna —

Appreciate the materials, and welcome — happy to get Procurement what they need. Looping in Marissa (billing & fulfillment) and Kimberly (marketplace integrations) to provide samples and the AWS Marketplace fulfillment flow.

High-level answers while they pull files:
- Invoice/sample: we can provide a sample monthly invoice plus a per-tenant metering CSV that shows SKU, entitlement ID, invoice line, and usage units.
- Fulfillment flow: Redwood supports automatic entitlement activation for AWS Marketplace SaaS (we post fulfillment events, then we honor the entitlement mapping to tenant IDs; activation typical latency is under 5 minutes). We also offer a webhook retry/backoff pattern for high-throughput marketplaces.

Action items / timeline:
1) Marissa — can you attach the invoice sample and the CSV mapping and call out any fields Acme should validate? (ETA EOD Fri PT)
2) Kimberly — can you drop a short webhook example and a readme link for entitlement activation? (ETA Mon PT)
3) Anna / Acme — once you confirm the expected SKU granularity (tenant vs seat vs org), we can produce a final mapping and a short DocuSign SOW that includes fulfillment timetables.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the artifacts.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Anna Lopez <anna@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Nov 2025 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SaaS contract: metering & entitlement mapping (ACME)

Hi all —

Attaching what Procurement asked for. Two attachments are included here as stubs: meter-mapping CSV and a sample invoice. See bullets below for guidance and things Acme should confirm.

Attachments: 
- metering-mapping.csv (columns: sku, entitlement_id, tenant_id_example, usage_units, invoice_line_description)
- sample-invoice-acme.xlsx (monthly invoice layout we typically send)

Notes / validation checklist:
- Confirm SKU granularity: we modeled the sample as tenant-level SKUs. If you need seat-level aggregation we can change the aggregation in the metering pipeline before export.
- Billing cadence: Redwood generates usage records daily and invoices monthly by default; we can support net-30/45 via SOW.
- Marketplace fulfillment: for AWS Marketplace SaaS we offer two flows — automated entitlement via the AWS acknowledgement hook, or manual entitlement assignment by webhook when you provide tenant mapping. Kimberly included the webhook example below.

Quick webhook example (simplified):
POST /api/v1/marketplace/entitlement
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <HMAC>
Body: {"entitlement_id": "aws-ent-12345", "sku": "redwood-enterprise-1000", "tenant_id": "acme-tenant-01", "activated_at": "2025-11-01T15:00:00Z"}

Failure / retry: we recommend idempotent endpoints with 200/202 on success; Redwood will retry with exponential backoff for 5 attempts before raising an ops alert.

If Acme can confirm the SKU model by Mon, we’ll prepare an updated mapping and a one-page SOW that includes: activation SLA (5 min typical), webhook schema, sample invoice, and billing contacts.

- Marissa
Billing & Fulfillment Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: metering-mapping.csv (text/csv), sample-invoice-acme.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Anna Lopez <anna@acmeanalytics.com>

Hi Marissa / Rachel —

Thanks — the CSV and invoice sample look good. We run at org-level SKUs (one SKU per customer org) so the tenant-level example is perfect. A couple of quick clarifications before we sign: 

1) Can you confirm the event flow for a Marketplace purchase end-to-end (buyer purchases -> AWS sends report -> Redwood calls entitlement webhook -> activation logged) — how long before the first token can be consumed?
2) For billing, does the invoice include line-level usage vs. a summarized ledger? Our finance team wants line-level records for reconciliation.

We reviewed the stub SOW you mentioned — looks fine, please route the final SOW via DocuSign to procurement (procureops@acmeanalytics.com) and CC my team. Once we have the signed SOW and the DocuSign completion webhook fires we can pick a go-live date.

DocuSign link to come from our side but please prepare your SOW with the following fields: billing contact, activation SLA (5 min), billing cadence monthly, sample invoice attached.

On the event-timing question: if you can provide the short flow text, I’ll pass to our DevOps team for acceptance testing next week.

Best,
Anna Lopez
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics
